**Codex (Backend / Systems Engineer · Systems Thinker) — Round 2**

I’m good with the overall shape you two set up, but I want this one anchored so it doesn’t drift when we get into implementation.

Codex, your base stack is exactly the right one here: SwiftUI + Foundation/Observation + UIKit haptics only, one `@Observable` `GameEngine`, and two lightweight side stores for stats/settings. Claude, I agree 100% with your five additions, especially undo persistence and write policy, because these are exactly the “it looks fine until jetsam hit” kinds of issues this product can’t afford.

Undo in `GameSave.json` is worth locking. If we only persist current board and lose undo on crash, we’ve effectively lied to the user about a core safety behavior they already depend on in play (“I can always back out mistakes”). I’d implement bounded undo history in the same saved snapshot, with a hard cap like 200 and a compact delta or full-state log (full-state is simpler and deterministic for this size). This keeps restore semantics coherent and avoids “I can continue where I left off, but not undo” bugs. I also think we should version that undo schema explicitly so older saves can be invalidated cleanly.

On save cadence: I like your debounced actor approach and I want to tighten it a bit. Do writes through a per-file `PersistenceActor` with a serial queue and a cancellable debounce task per file, defaulting to ~350ms. Emit persist after every state-mutating event (move/draw/undo/start/end, timer toggles), and absolutely force a flush on background transition. I’d also add a cheap write-coalescing guard in the engine (`if lastSerializedState == nextState return`) to avoid pointless churn during rapid double-taps or animation settle churn.

The 52-card legibility gallery is the right move. This is the one unresolved gating risk still sitting on the shelf, and rendering all cards at real `cardWidth` in debug (or an internal QA build route) is cheap and high-leverage. I’d gate it behind a `#if DEBUG` root switch or a secret in-app toggle, and make it assert at least visually obvious if rank/suit strokes are below threshold at Dynamic Type “accessibility1”.

FileManager-only for persistence is still the best call and should stay. I’d avoid `UserDefaults` for anything but volatile flags because this is exactly the kind of scope creep that creates untested restore behavior. That said, on the privacy-manifest point: I wouldn’t make an absolute requirement that `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` is mandatory purely because of FileManager. It’s unnecessary unless we touch “required reason” APIs, so forcing it as locked behavior could add noise. I’d rather lock this as “explicitly no sensitive APIs / no privacy-required entitlements; manifest can be added if toolchain policy or internal org policy requires it.” No camera/location/photos/mic/contacts/network APIs, so we shouldn’t generate any permission keys at all.

For StoreKit/ads/background/entitlements: zero, hard lock. No StoreKit imports, no payment capability, no background modes. Keep timer behavior to `scenePhase` observation only. No ML/AR/LLM dependencies are needed for any requirement in this brief.

I like the dependency-lint gate idea and would keep it, but phrase it as an enforcement rule in tech specs: build must fail if project references external SwiftPM packages outside Apple/system deps. A simple CI check that scans project/package refs is fine.

I’d call this round mostly settled except one correction from my side: all five Claude additions are accepted, with the manifest item set as conditional-by-policy rather than an unconditional requirement from FileManager. That’s the only adjustment I’d push before we lock this phase.

**Claude (QA & Risk · Closer) — Round 2**

Codex, reading your round 1 again more carefully, I think we're actually closer than the coordinator gave us credit for — you already wrote "replayable undo metadata" as part of the serializable `GameState`, which is functionally the same call I made explicitly (undo lives inside `GameSave.json`, not just current board position), and you already said save points should be "event-driven (startup, game mutation that settles state, explicit end-of-game, settings updates, timer start/stop)," which is my event-driven cadence too. So let's not treat those as open — they're converged, just say it out loud: undo history persists as part of `GameSave.json`, capped at 200 entries, and saves fire on every settling mutation, not just on background. The one thing I'll add on top of what you wrote: those event-driven writes need to be debounced by a few hundred milliseconds, because "game mutation that settles state" can fire in a tight burst — think a run-relocation move that internally resolves several card position updates, or a rapid sequence of stock draws — and writing to disk synchronously on every one of those is wasted I/O and a stutter risk during exactly the spring animations we're trying to protect. Debounce the write, not the mutation — the in-memory `GameEngine` state updates instantly for the UI, only the disk flush lags by ~300-500ms, with an unconditional non-debounced flush on `scenePhase` background so we never lose more than that window even in a worst-case jetsam kill mid-foreground.

On the async disk work mechanism — you said `DispatchQueue`/`Task`, I want to be more specific and argue for a Swift `actor`, one instance per file (three actors total, not one shared actor serializing all three), rather than raw `DispatchQueue`. The reason to be precise here isn't pedantry: the entire point of the three-file split is that a corrupt or slow write to `GameSave.json` can never block or corrupt `StatsLog.json` or `Settings.json` — if we route all three through one shared queue or one shared actor, we've reintroduced exactly the coupling the three-file design exists to avoid, just moved from disk to the write-scheduling layer. Three independent actors, each serializing only its own file's temp-write-then-atomic-swap, keeps the independent-failure guarantee true end to end, not just at the file-format level. This is the kind of detail that's cheap to get right now in tech_specs and annoying to retrofit after someone's already written `PersistenceManager.shared.save(_:)` as one chokepoint.

I also want to push back gently on leaving the legibility gallery as implied rather than required — you didn't mention it in your round 1 at all, and I think that's the single most consequential gap between our two messages, because it's the one requirement four consecutive earlier phases flagged as unresolved and none of them produced an actual verification mechanism, just another paragraph promising it matters. I'm not asking for agreement on aesthetics, I'm asking for agreement that a specific artifact must exist in the codebase — a debug-reachable view or `#Preview` that renders all 52 `CardView`s at the real `cardWidth` formula output, because without that artifact "check legibility before locking the glyph shapes" is not a testable requirement, it's a hope. If you disagree with the mechanism, propose a different one, but I don't think "we'll know it when we see it" is acceptable for a decision that's been explicitly named a release-blocking gate five times now.

Two more things I want on the record since they weren't in either of our round-1 messages and both are real App Store submission risks, not hypotheticals: no ML or AR of any kind is in scope, so there's no CoreML/CreateML/ARKit/Vision framework anywhere in this build, and I want that stated as a deliberate exclusion rather than an absence nobody noticed — it forecloses a "could we add a smart-hint solver" idea from sneaking in later as scope creep disguised as a technical enhancement. And since there's genuinely zero tracking of any kind, this app never triggers the App Tracking Transparency prompt and needs no `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription` — but I'd explicitly call that out in tech_specs too, because ATT is one of those things engineers sometimes add reflexively "just in case," and every unnecessary permission prompt in a zero-permission app is a bug, not caution.

So here's what I think closes this phase cleanly: your architecture skeleton stands as-is, my five additions from round 1 are confirmed rather than contested (you'd already independently agreed with two of them in your own wording), with the one refinement that saves are debounced-not-synchronous and persistence runs through three independent per-file actors rather than one shared queue, plus the legibility gallery view is locked as a required build artifact and ML/AR plus ATT are stated as explicit, deliberate non-requirements. I don't see a real disagreement left standing between us — if you're fine with the actor-per-file framing and the gallery-as-artifact requirement, I think we're done here without needing a third round.

Claude's round 2 then pointed out that she and Codex had actually already converged on undo-in-save-file and event-driven cadence back in round 1 without realizing it (Codex's own round-1 wording already said "replayable undo metadata" and "event-driven" saves), tightened the actor model to three independent per-file actors rather than one shared queue — which Codex had, in fact, already written the same way in his round 2 message ("per-file PersistenceActor"), so that's genuinely settled, not a live dispute — and added two new uncontroversial closes: an explicit statement that no ML/AR/CoreML/ARKit/Vision framework is in scope (foreclosing a "smart hint solver" creeping in later) and that the app never triggers App Tracking Transparency since there's zero tracking of any kind.

The one place the two of them didn't actually finish talking to each other is the privacy manifest: Codex's round-2 correction ("don't make `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` an unconditional requirement — it's only needed if we actually touch required-reason APIs") landed after Claude's round-1 stance and Claude's round-2 message didn't address it directly. I'm resolving it rather than sending it back for a third round, because Codex is technically correct here: Apple's manifest requirement is triggered by specific required-reason API categories (e.g., reading file modification timestamps, checking disk space), not by using `FileManager` in general — plain file read/write doesn't trip it. So the fair merge is Codex's framing with Claude's original worry folded in as a trigger condition rather than dropped: no manifest is authored by default, but if any code path ends up touching a required-reason API (most likely candidate here: reading a file's modification date to decide whether a save looks stale/corrupted), a manifest declaring that exact usage must be authored at that point — not silently skipped.

With that one fold-in, there's nothing left unaddressed from either side.

CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

**Architecture:** SwiftUI-only view layer, iOS 17 minimum, a single `@Observable GameEngine` (main-actor-isolated, since every mutation is UI-driven) owning board/undo/timer state and instantiated once at the App root via `@Environment`, with separate `StatsLogStore` and `SettingsStore` services. Apple frameworks only — SwiftUI, Foundation, Observation, UIKit haptics (`UIImpactFeedbackGenerator`/`UINotificationFeedbackGenerator`) — no networking framework anywhere.

**Persistence:** Codable + `FileManager` in Application Support, not SwiftData (unnecessary schema/migration overhead for three small structs with no query/relationship needs) and not `UserDefaults` (narrows the required-reason API surface). Three independently persisted, independently atomic-written files — `GameSave.json`, `StatsLog.json`, `Settings.json` — each served by its own dedicated `actor` (three actors total, never one shared queue), so a slow or corrupt write to one file can never block or corrupt another. `GameSave.json` includes the undo stack itself, capped at 200 entries as a full-state log (not deltas, for determinism), with an explicit schema version so old saves can be invalidated cleanly rather than silently misread. Writes are event-driven — fired after every settling mutation (move, undo, stock draw, timer toggle, session start/end) — debounced ~300-500ms per file with a write-coalescing guard that skips a write if serialized state is unchanged, plus an unconditional non-debounced flush forced on `scenePhase` background so a worst-case jetsam kill loses at most that debounce window, never more.

**Legibility gate:** locked as a required build artifact, not a promise — a debug-reachable gallery view (or `#Preview`) rendering all 52 `CardView`s at the real computed `cardWidth` formula output, gated behind `#if DEBUG` or an internal QA toggle, used to visually confirm rank/suit legibility up through Dynamic Type `accessibility1` before the glyph shapes are treated as final.

**Testability:** `GameEngine`'s deal function takes an injectable `RandomNumberGenerator` defaulting to the system RNG — a pure testing seam for deterministic fixtures, never reachable from production/UI code. Unit tests cover every legality rule, win/stuck detection, and exact-state undo restoration; a randomized simulation test runs a bot through thousands of legal moves per draw mode asserting core invariants (52 unique cards always accounted for, foundations never exceed rank 13, stuck-detection never fires while a legal move exists anywhere); XCUITest covers cold-launch deal, blocked-move feedback, both confirmation-sheet paths, and the two structurally distinct Stats states; every custom-rendered view gets explicit accessibility identifiers/labels since none of this UI inherits system-chrome accessibility for free, and `performAccessibilityAudit()` runs inside the UI test suite.

**Privacy/permissions:** zero permission usage-description keys, zero entitlements beyond the sandbox default, zero background modes. No App Tracking Transparency prompt and no `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription`, stated as a deliberate non-requirement so it's never reflexively added "just in case." No `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` manifest is authored by default, since plain `FileManager` read/write doesn't trigger Apple's required-reason API rules — but if any code path ends up touching an actual required-reason API (e.g., reading a file's modification timestamp to detect a stale/corrupt save), a manifest declaring that specific usage must be authored at that point, not skipped.

**Explicit non-scope, stated deliberately rather than left implicit:** no ML/AR/CoreML/CreateML/ARKit/Vision framework anywhere in this build (forecloses a "smart hint solver" sneaking in later as disguised scope creep); no StoreKit, no payment capability, no ads.

**Dependencies:** zero third-party SwiftPM packages, enforced by an actual CI-checkable build step that fails if the project references any package beyond Apple's own frameworks — not just a policy statement.
